lessons.prompt:
I'm working through "Set the Sprint Goal & Select Stories" (Build → Iteration Planning) on my own project. Act as my assistant: draft and check, I decide.

Goal: Give the sprint one reason to exist and select only the stories that serve it.
Done looks like: A single, outcome-worded sprint goal and the ordered selection of Ready stories that reach it within the forecast.

I'll attach or paste: Capacity plan; Ready stories; Product backlog.

Work through these steps with me, one at a time:
1. Propose a goal worded as an outcome → Sprint goal
2. Select Ready stories that serve it → Iteration backlog
3. Split stories too big for the sprint → Ready backlog item
4. Estimate and compare with the forecast → Iteration backlog
5. Goal reachable within the forecast? (a decision — give me the options and a recommendation; I make the call)

Produce: Sprint goal; Iteration backlog. Use clear headings I can paste into my document.

Ask me for anything you need instead of guessing. Keep it specific to my project.

lessons.title: Break Stories into Tasks & Commit the Sprint
lessons.summary: Split stories into day-sized tasks, give each story an owner and freeze the commitment.

definition.purpose: Make all the work visible on day one and fix the plan, so any later change is a deliberate, recorded decision.
definition.outcome: A task breakdown including tests, instrumentation and docs, a lane owner per story and a frozen sprint commitment.
definition.jtbd: Help me see every piece of work I'm signing up for and know the plan won't shift under me without a reason.
exit: Commitment recorded with lanes, date and revision 0

normal: Add test, instrumentation, migration and docs tasks
parallel: Tasking of different stories in parallel by pairs

cases.happyPath: Tasks fit, every story has an owner and the team commits.
alternates: Swarm: several people on one story, one lane owner still accountable

exceptions: Task reveals behaviour no criterion covers → back to refinement
failures: Tests left out of the tasks

routing.alternate: Swarming → one accountable owner per story, many contributors
routing.rework: Task shows the story is not Ready → back to refinement (re-plan)
routing.escalation: Dependency on another team → delivery lead
routing.stop: Committed stories cannot be built (e.g. environment down) → do not commit; re-plan the sprint — recorded in the learning log

lessons.title: Track the Sprint, Re-plan with a Reason & Close
lessons.summary: Inspect progress daily, clear blockers, change the commitment only by reasoned re-plan, then review and retrospect.

definition.purpose: Keep the sprint on course to its goal, make every scope change explicit and end with feedback and improvement.
definition.outcome: A sprint whose changes are all recorded re-plans, closed with a review of done work and a retrospective with owned actions.
definition.jtbd: Help me raise problems early, change course openly and finish the sprint having learned something.
exit: Every change recorded as a re-plan
Review held; retrospective actions owned and in the learning log

normal: Propose a re-plan when the commitment no longer fits
parallel: Blocker resolution runs alongside the work
flow.stateTransitions: Committed → In progress → (Re-planned rev n) → Reviewed → Closed

cases.happyPath: No re-plan needed; goal met; review and retro held.
alternates: Re-plan swaps a blocked story for an equal Ready one
Kanban: replenishment meeting instead of re-plan
exceptions: External blocker (vendor sandbox down) → re-plan with reason

routing.forward: Done increments → 4.6.4 Check the Definition of Done & Hand Off; retro actions → learning log
routing.alternate: Equal swap keeps the goal → accept re-plan
routing.rework: Blocker unresolved for a day → re-plan
routing.escalation: Goal no longer reachable → product owner; sponsor if a date is at risk
routing.stop: Goal obsolete → cancel the sprint; re-plan from scratch — recorded in the learning log

criteria: Every change has a re-plan record with a reason
checks: Burndown read at the daily scrum
rules: No silent scope change
Only done work shown at review

decisions: Do we change the plan?

agents: AI agent proposing re-plan change sets
execution.authority: Agents may propose re-plans; only a person accepts them; cancelling a sprint is the product owner's call.

continuity.handoff: Re-plan records → sprint board; review notes → product backlog; retro → learning log → EVOLVE
traceability: SPR-## revisions list added / removed STY-###; LRN-### linked to SPR-##
continuity.timebox: Daily 15 min; re-plan 15 min; review and retro 2–3 hours
learning: Causes of re-plans; retro actions — learning log
